reason: Machine lens: test-assembled in a scratch copy (plain and gameplay flag sets), both assemble with every ASSERT passing; hazel_b_end &DF65 -> &DF90, mgame_end &4E61. All opcodes are 65SC12-valid (INC A = &1A, no Rockwell/WDC bit ops); section is cmos = TRUE. Whole routine &DF4A-&DF8F sits in page &DF, so no branch crosses a page; BNE row is -62 (in range). sky_r* tables at &BC90-&BCB9 with X <= 5: no indexed page crossing. sky_col_check is the last code of hazel_b; only the copied load image after it slides (no self-modified operands or page-aligned code there; sky_col_row, still used by sky_col_zero and sky_edges, is untouched). Equivalence checked against source: entry tests match sky_col_row's (sk > ry -> next, sk == ry passes); the builder gives rn = L+1 with rt = L (bottom), rn = 8 rt = 7 (middle), rn 1..8 rt = 7 (top, n >= 1 since H > 8), split copies keep rt and rn, so rt|sk - rn + 1 never borrows and s_ptr + Y covers exactly the old rl/rh + Y addresses (16-bit sums identical). rc is a multiple of 8 even for split entries (rl is). s_ptr, sky_stop, Y, A differ on exit but every later reader (sky_row, sky_col_row) writes them first. Page crossings on (s_ptr),Y can only fall (new base >= old base, same addresses). Cycles recounted per in-range row: old 71 + 15*rn, new 62 + 10*rn (+1 when sk == ry; rn = 1: 86 -> 74). Measured 2.3 rows and 14.1 bytes a pass: about 2.3*9 + 14.1*5 = 91 a pass, ~40 a row, matching the claim. Bytes: 27 -> 70, 43 more (claim's -43).
